author: Y Combinator
description:
Should governments intervene to substantially slow the progress of frontier AI? In the inaugural YC debate, Jacob Coxon, an ex-Anthropic and OpenAI researcher, faces off against Robin Hanson, an economist at GMU, about AI takeoff and what government regulation should (or shouldn’t) do about it.

Chapters:
00:00 - YC Debate Topic: Should We Slow Down AI?
02:42 - Jacob's case: Superintelligence by 2028
07:02 - Models already behaving in ways we don't understand
09:18 - Robin's case: the danger of abstraction
11:22 - Why new technologies take decades to diffuse
13:12 - Liability instead of regulation
14:50 - Why regulating AI is different from regulating drugs
16:00 - Jacob's rebuttal: general intelligence is one number
17:36 - Why normal liability won't cover extinction risk
19:52 - Robin's rebuttal: regulating this means regulating all compute
21:44 - AI as our descendants
23:38 - Diminishing returns
24:40 - Direct exchange: is it just the rate of change?
